title: Paranal beneath the Milky Way
caption: The Milky Way over Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Milky Way fills the sky above the Chilean Atacama Desert, while ESO's Very Large Telescope sits far off in the distance on top of Cerro Paranal. The telescopes look tiny beneath the glowing band of our galaxy.

ESO presents the photograph as proof of how clear the night sky is at this site. The summit of Cerro Paranal stands 2600 metres high. That clarity is the reason the Very Large Telescope was built here, as part of the Paranal Observatory.

For any large observatory, the quality of the sky matters a great deal. Clouds and haze get in the way of faint starlight, so a site with unusually clear nights gives telescopes a better chance of recording dim, distant objects. The Milky Way arching over the desert here is the evidence ESO points to.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera in the Atacama Desert. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure collects much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way appears brighter and more detailed here than it would to a person on the spot.
